text.p: These are the leading stories in the Kenyan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Opposition parliamentarians Paul Muite and Kiraitu Murungi say they will sue Kenya police for assault after being beaten at a public rally in Nyeri.
- Professor Arthur Obel says he will not sell what he says is the anti-HIV Pearl Omega drug because it has been banned.
- The mayor of Nakuru says she fears for her life after receiving threats from a leader of the ruling Kenya National African Party.
- Cabinet minister Nicholas Biwott witnesses the passing of a declaration for the government to ensure security so victims of clashes in the Rift Valley can return to their homes.
- A furore rages over FORD-Kenya opposition party Chairman Michael Wamalwa's correspondence with business tycoon Ketan Somaia.
- The Prince of Wales will this Easter bring his two sons William and Harry to Kenya, for a historic visit.
- Opposition Democratic Party parliamentarian Kennedy Kiliku declares interest in vying for the presidency of Kenya.
- More than 12 heavily-armed gangsters raid a sawmill and murder two watchmen.
- Four people are arrested in Lodwar town on suspicion of stealing food aid. ($1=54 Kenyan Shillings)
